title: Television control experiment (30 subjects, 4 classes, 31 EEG ch)
description: EEG recordings from 30 healthy participants performing an online P300-based brain-computer interface task for controlling a television. Participants attended to flashing visual stimuli in a 4-class oddball paradigm shown on an LCD display. Data were recorded from 31 EEG channels at 500 Hz, with 50 training and 30 testing blocks per subject. The dataset was designed to support home appliance control and inter-subject transfer learning research.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with an actiCHamp (Brain Products) amplifier using 31 active electrodes placed according to the 10-20 system, referenced to linked mastoids, at a 500 Hz sampling rate. Visual flash stimuli were presented on an LCD with a 750 ms stimulus onset asynchrony. Each subject completed 50 training and 30 testing blocks in a single session with online visual feedback.
